newsitem.title: USA: Dow slammed in biggest point loss since mid-July.
newsitem.headline: Dow slammed in biggest point loss since mid-July.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average skidded 79 points Tuesday to its biggest point loss since a July sell-off as investors raced to lock in profits after a spectacular November.

"A wave of sell programmes hit the market. Big stocks were punished and small caps performed somewhat better. It appears there was profit-taking after a superb month of market action in November," said Alan Ackerman, a market strategist at Fahnestock and Co.

The Dow industrials shed 79.01 points, or 1.21 percent, to close at 6,442.69 as it was hit by a huge sell programme in a frantic last 10 minutes of trading. It was the blue chip index's biggest point drop since July 15's 161.05-point slump amid heightened earnings jitters.
The Dow soared about 500 points, or 8 percent, in November and many were awaiting a pullback.
In the broader market, gainers beat losers 1,294 to 1,192 on very heavy volume of about 516 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The broader market also ended well off its highs, although the technology-studded Nasdaq Composite clung to minor gains that helped it set its seventh consecutive record. The index rose 0.55 to 1,300.37, its first finish above 1,300.
"This is the type of blow-off the market needs to take a little wind out of the sails," said Douglas Myers of Interstate Johnson/Lane. "Give it a chance to rebalance, reallocate and wax philosophic."
Bellwether International Business Machines Corp., which hit a nine-year high earlier in the day of 166, ended down 1/8 at 163-1/8 -- its first lower close in about two weeks.
Among other Dow components, General Electric Co. lost 4 to 99-1/4, Procter & Gamble shed 3-7/8 to 104-3/4 and United Technologies was off 3-1/2 to 136-1/2.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose 1/32, leaving its yield unchanged at 6.36 percent.

Bond prices hit the day's highs after news that seasonally adjusted new single-family homes sales fell a surprisingly sharp 8.7 percent in October. But Treasuries turned lower later as the market was hit by a spate of corporate bond offerings, including $850 million of IBM 100-year debentures.

Interest-rate sensitive stocks came under more selling pressure after enjoying recent strong gains. Wells Fargo lost 4-1/4 to 279-1/2, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. shed 3 to 111-5/8 and BankAmerica was off 3 to 98-3/4.
Among individual shares, Hutchinson Technology soared 19-1/2 to 72-1/4 after forecasting that first-quarter ended Dec. 29 earnings would far exceed analysts' expectations.
Silicon Graphics surged 3-3/8 to 23-5/8 after Goldman Sachs recommended the stock, upgrading it from market performer.
U.S. Robotics tumbled 7-1/8 to 73-3/4 after Needham & Co. cautioned that the modem maker may be facing a weak quarter as it shifts to new technology, market sources said. Needham declined to comment.
Summit Technology added 2-3/8 to 8-3/4. Summit said the government approved its plan to expand clinical trials using a laser system to treat farsightedness.
Centocor surged 5-3/8 to 34-3/8. Morgan Stanley raised its price target and Salomon reiterated its strong buy.
Market Facts surged 8-1/4 to 42-3/4. The provider of custom market research cited an increased awareness of the stock among investors and additional market makers.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks fell 8.28 points to 748.28.
The NYSE composite index of all listed common stocks slid 3.29 to 394.85. The average price per share fell 35 cents.
The American Stock Exchange index fell 0.75 to 592.18.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,250.456, down 45.113, or 0.62 percent.
